strings.SAM_THENEWORDER_DESC:
Born of hazy post-war plans, the Russian Liberation Army, or ROA, was envisioned as nothing more than a collaborator militia writ large. Led by General Vlasov and a collection of turncoat Red Army officers, the ROA was meant to help legitimize German control of RK Moskowien until the Russians could be driven further east or exterminated.

The West Russian War in the fifties changed all of this. Expanded by the desperate Germans and deployed to delay the resurgent Red Army, the ROA thrived against all odds and soon found itself pushing east. By the war's end, Vlasov and his men controlled a power base beyond the Reich's grasp. Written off as mutinous rabble, the ROA has spent the intervening years waiting. Some hope for redemption; the others merely await the opportunity to carve an empire in Western Russia and beyond.

strings.SAM_CountryInfo_Content_desc.1: In the bloodiest days of the West Russian War, when it seemed like the Reich's hold on Russia was on the verge of slipping forever, the German high command turned to desperate means to stave off the collapse of their front line. Drawn from a range of auxiliary colonial militias of Russian conscripts that were meant to police German-held Russia, the Russian Liberation Army or ROA was created. In propaganda, the ROA was depicted as a proud Russian army, fighting the Bolshevik menace of the West Russian Revolutionary Front. In desperation, the Germans even allowed the creation of the Committee for the Liberation of the Peoples of Russia, or KONR, as the embryo of a free Russian Republic that would rule over areas liberated by the German counter offensives.
strings.SAM_CountryInfo_Content_desc.2: Reality was much less flattering to the ROA. Its leader Andrey Vlasov, a former Red Army general, was nothing more than a puppet of the Wehrmacht's high command. His officers were a disjointed bunch. Many were also captured Red Army officers, preferring to join the ROA than die in a German POW camp. Others were fascist émigrés, joining the ROA on a great crusade to defeat Bolshevism. The common soldiers were desperate cannon fodder, drafted at gunpoint by the Germans and sent to reinforce the most desperate sectors of the front. Far from being welcomed as liberators, Russian people caught in the conflict area welcomed ROA soldiers with rock and insults.
strings.SAM_CountryInfo_Content_desc.3: Despite all this, the ROA pushed on. The soldiers fought with the energy of desperation, and managed to help turn the tide in the sector around Samara. Soon the ROA found itself beyond the German lines, freed from their former taskmasters. With the war winding down and the WRRF in retreat, the Germans wrote off their cannon fodder as mutinous Slav Untermensch. The new headquarters of the ROA in Samara were not spared any of the terror bombing campaigns that followed. Since then the ROA has huddled in Samara, having traded one prison for another. Unable to expand their area of control by the terror bombings, and forbidden to go back home in the west, the common soldiers of the army have languished for the better part of a decade in their garrisons.
strings.SAM_CountryInfo_Content_desc.4: The ROA's officers, meanwhile, have grown weary of Vlasov's indecisiveness. They argue for a more decentralized leadership, and for the abandonment of KONR's original democratic mission in favor of a continuation of the ROA's junta. Using General Sergei Bunyachenko as their mouthpiece, the men of the Officers' Committee scheme to take advantage of Vlasov's apathy and old age. However the officers are not all united in ideology. Quite a few have formed a pro-democracy faction, and argue that Vlasov's heir as chairman of KONR should be Miletiy Zykov, a former journalist that has maneuvered his way into being the chief propagandist of the ROA's regime in Samara. Zykov argues for the continued struggle to liberate Russia from Bolshevism as well as German oppression. In between all this, many common soldiers and lower ranking officers have grown tired of the high command's bickering and seek to follow General Artsezo's goal to use the ROA to build a strong, fascist state... and to enrich the soldiers in the process.
strings.SAM_CountryInfo_Content_desc.5: The ROA is at a crossroad. Loathed by all their neighbors as German collaborators, yet feared for their veteran army and iron discipline, the men of the ROA await the end of the terror bombing. Some seek to redeem their honor by rebuilding Russia. Others seek vengeance on the communists and on the Germans who have ruined their life. Finally, a growing minority simply want to lash out at the uncaring world that has forced them to lose a decade holed in Samara.
strings.SAM_german_bootlickers_desc: As much as we like to claim that we are a spearhead for the Liberation of Russia from under the Red Yoke of Bolshevism, everybody considers us an extension of German influence over the Motherland, and correspondingly hate us for it. Unfortunately, hatred by the Russian people does not correspond to love from our former German masters, who have written us off as mutinous rabble.
strings.SAM_The_Smolensk_Manifesto_desc: Proof of the ROA's legitimacy to a select few, and a proof of their irredeemable treachery for all else. The Manifesto was issued during the West Russian War, declaring the ROA's opposition to communism in Russia and hopes for a new republic to replace the Soviet Union. Despite its creation by the hands of desperate German propagandists, the manifesto has remained a core component of our claim to legitimacy.
strings.SAM_The_Samara_Manifesto_desc: In order to legitimize the ROA as an organization that hopes to unite the Russian people under one banner, the obsolete Smolensk Declaration has been discarded, and a new declaration, titled the Samara Manifesto, has been written. This declaration denounces foreign influence within Russian politics and pledges to make Russia whole under a strong and independent government.
strings.SAM_German_Military_Training_desc: Back when the ROA was a mere colonial militia, the Germans insisted on imposing military training and savage discipline onto their subhuman auxiliaries. The West Russian War saw the army's numbers swell with former Red Army veterans, and their mettle tested in desperate battles. As such, the ROA is one of the few professional militaries in Western Russia.
strings.SAM_Turncoat_General_desc: Our generals and officers share little in common beyond their past as Germans prisoners of war and a willingness to work with the Germans. Some were driven by a hatred of the Red Army or anger at bad treatment, real or imagined. Others simply saw it as the way out of a prisoners' camp. No matter the reason, and no matter how skilled they are, our generals' treason to the Russian people make them widely detested men.
strings.SAM_Village_Councils_desc:
Rural Russia has long looked to itself for governance. Communes remain the principal government apparatus at the local level.

A system of military attachés to village councils has been developed. Slowly but surely, local communities are moving away from seeing garrisons as predatory or parasitic organizations. In turn local commanders are being scrutinized more and more for their ability to maintain peace and prosperity within their assigned area.
strings.SAM_Bread_for_All_desc: The bare minimum for any man or woman to survive is nourishment. While this will put a dent into our resources, providing our people the bare minimum isn't just a necessity, but a duty. If the people of Samara are to face the future tribulations ahead, it must be with a full belly.
strings.SAM_Soup_for_Service_desc: Our resources are stretched thin as is, and it's no time for compassion or charity. Simply put, those that put the work, will be given what is due. Those that don't, or leech from us, will not. Food is a privilege to those that deserve it, and it's due that people are reminded of that.
strings.SAM_slipped_leash_desc: Well, well, would you look at this; the German rulership decayed enough to finally let us assert ourselves as a power in our own right. This golden opportunity will not be left to go to waste; our highly-trained force will reach out, unite the other Russian warlords then drive out the Teutons with their own weapons! They will rue the day they stepped foot into Russia when they see their very own former lapdogs leading the charge against them!
strings.SAM_Bureaucratic_Allies_idea_desc: It is said the right man in the right place makes all the difference in the world. The cooperation between us and the Officer Committee, once dominated by bickering and red tape walling, now is smooth sailing, our requests and proposals being processed at a lightning speed. It is not anymore a matter if our necessities will be attended by the officers, but a when.
strings.SAM_Renewed_Military_Trust_desc:
The Samaran government has never been popular. At best, our people grudgingly tolerated us for our anti-bandit efforts.

Things have begun changing for the better. Stricter discipline for soldiers as well as an ongoing anti-corruption campaign have shown the population that the days of army officers lording over peasants like boyars of old are ending. People now hope they can trust their army.
strings.SAM_The_ROA_is_MINE_desc: With the opposition either jumping ship, or increasingly irrelevant, Artsezo is the decisive leader of the ROA. Nothing inside Samara happens without his knowledge, and nothing ever will, if he has any say in the matter.
strings.SAM_Russia_in_my_Sights_desc: Russia is ripe for the taking, and there's no time to be lost. Under the allure of profit and wealth, Artsezo will unleash the dogs of war upon West Russia. Time is wasting, and there's profit to be made.
strings.SAM_gunsmithing_desc: Russia will not be won with antiquated weaponry and jury rigged equipment. A proper manufacturing drive has been set, to arm our soldiers with the finest, modern equipment we can muster. Our enemies will not find us fighting with antiquated peashoters, but the finest crafts of war Russia has seen.
strings.SAM_gunsmithing2_desc: Past are the days that we were but one of many rump states across this land. We are fulfilling the task we set to do since the Patriotic War. Hand-picked gunsmiths work tirelessly, on the homefront of innovation, while keeping in mind our budget for the other needs of our nation. And perhaps, one day, our weapons will be seen on the same level as the other superpowers.
strings.SAM_Russian_Industry_desc: The factories churn on a daily basis the materials and supplies of not only the liberation of West Russia but perhaps even the distant dream of a fully united Russia. No longer will the ROA soldier deal with makeshift, old guns from the '40s, and smuggled supplies, but with genuine Russian equipment. While the dream of a fully united Russia under her truthful sons and daughters is a distant dream, the end of the contemptible warlords around us is a reality we live in now, and a fact if we hold steadfast.
strings.SAM_Motorized_Contracts_idea_desc: During the Second World War, and the West Russian War, war is all about the momentum. Our soldiers must not strike at our foes on foot, but on the highest quality automobile our private contractors can muster. Russia will not be won only through foot, but through the thunderous roar of our engines!
strings.SAM_The_Zykov_Plan_Complete_desc:
In a bid to prepare their statelet for war, KONR has decided to implement Miletiy Zykov's development plan.

Using joint civilian-military development initiatives, the economic renewal plan has seen the agricultural sector stabilized and a more complex industrial sector emerge. In the meantime the Army of Liberation itself has seen reforms meant to better integrate its Moskowien originating core with local recruits.
strings.SAM_The_Committee_Plan_Completed_desc: Where once laid apathy and stillness, there is momentum. Every able worker works dutifully, and our industry flourishes, producing more daily. Like a bolder rolling down a hill, inertia was beaten, and our momentum can only pick up pace. Let all those that stand in our way be crushed!
strings.SAM_The_Officer_Plan_Completed_desc: Samara is a gem, and Artsezo and his officers knew all it took was to clean the dirt and a little elbow grease to make it shine. Distributed equally between his collaborators, Samara is ready to be the pride jewel of Artsezo's Russia. Now, to bring about the other jewels...

Russia has always struggled to industrialize. The Tsars' attempts failed, leading to their defeat to the Germans and the rise of the accursed Bolsheviks. They were little better, with little growth in heavy industries needed to resist the Nazi anslaught. We will learn from their failures, and properly industrialize with the help of large corporate entities - the Kombinats - and limited state intervention. With private and public interests working together to develop Russia, a bright and prosperous future for the Russian people is within our grasp.
strings.SAM_zykov_ROA_dominant_desc: The Officer Committee and their representative Bunyachenko have become the dominant faction in Samara. Always the strongest grouping within the ROA, it seems that the committee pushes to continue the junta indefinitely. That said, many within Samara's power circles have noticed some new life within General Bunyachenko. Perhaps the Ukrainian born general has some designs of his own?
strings.SAM_zykov_business_dominant_desc: More and more power within Samara is centered on commander Artsezo's faction. Having amassed vast amount of influence through his control of smuggling networks, the affable smuggler officer has amassed a kernel of corrupt officials, ultranationalist demagogues and pragmatic men around him to secure a growing hold on the capital.
strings.SAM_zykov_democrats_dominant_desc: Against all odds, Zykov's faction of democrats has become dominant within the ROA. Backed by young officers as well as civilian leaders, Miletiy Zykov now maintains a strong influence within the various groups. All speculate on the enigmatic propagandist's true intentions, but his actions have so far been coherent with his claimed hopes of liberalization and democratization.

strings.SAM_military_morale_low_desc:
The Russian Liberation Army would not get far in its quest for national liberation without its armed men. Yet our current army morale is low.

Veterans from Moskowien miss home, and worry about their family. Their younger comrades find conscription into an army of traitors repulsive. Supplies are low, pay is poor. Many officers avoid the barracks out of fear of mutinous troops.
strings.SAM_military_morale_medium_desc:
The cause of Russian liberation is a noble one. It is also made possible as long as our men believe in this dream. Our current army morale is medium.

Troops tend to their work with efficiency, if not enthusiasm. Conscription is augmented by a smattering of volunteers, attracted by better living conditions. Veterans grumble from time to time that back during the West Russian War their rations were much more inedible.
strings.SAM_military_morale_high_desc:
From humble beginnings, the army of national liberation has evolved into a disciplined, motivated force. Our current army morale is high.

Soldiers tend to their work energetically. Good pay and good conditions attract more and more men to our cause. Veterans from Moskowien dare dream of home, to get through their darkest nights.
strings.SAM_military_morale_very_high_desc:
Men will fight to survive, but few will for a cause they do not believe in. Our military morale is currently very high.

The army of Russian liberation is currently one of the best motivated armies in Western Russia. Well fed, well equipped, and well trained, our soldiers wait impatiently for the chance to liberate our homeland from petty warlordism.
strings.SAM_civilian_morale_low_desc:
Our army claims to fight to liberate the people of Russia. Alas, our current civilian morale is low.

People living within areas we administer find their lives nasty, brutish and short. Food shortages, predatory taxation rackets ran by local soldiers and a general breakdown of law and order make the life of the population hellish. All curse the day the German dogs of the ROA slipped their leash.
strings.SAM_civilian_morale_medium_desc:
Life is hard within the Russian Anarchy. Nevertheless, civilian morale within our land is medium.

As within most statelets of the former Soviet Union, most of the resources are seized for the army's needs. Nevertheless the average citizen has a roof over their head and enough food to feed their family. The ROA, while unpopular, is seen as a tolerable alternative to life under German rule, for now...
strings.SAM_civilian_morale_high_desc:
Statecraft is a difficult science. Nonetheless our motley array of civilian and military administrators have managed to raise civilian morale to high.

Our lands are generally safe from banditry, its people broadly prosperous. Tax is collected in a fair way. Citizens are protected from law breaking soldiers... Most of the time. Our people begrudgingly find our rule competent and legitimate.
strings.SAM_civilian_morale_very_high_desc:
From the ashes we have built up a successful polity. Current civilian morale is very high.

Life within our nation is considered as good as it can get in Russia these days. Where our citizens were once apathetic to our rule, many now catch themselves hoping for continued ROA successes. Many communities are now generating surpluses. Our people go to sleep with full stomachs, dreaming of a better future.
strings.SAM_corruption_low_desc:
Sincerity is the way of Heaven. Our current corruption level is low.

Paralegal means can be helpful in the Russian Anarchy, where governmental resources are often stretched thin. Nevertheless, our state has cracked down on most sources of corruption. While this may make our dealings with Moskowien harder, it also secures our control of the army by removing competing poles of power.
strings.SAM_corruption_medium_desc:
By nature, men are nearly alike; by practice, they get to be wide apart. Our current level of corruption is medium.

Corruption is a fact of life in the Russian Anarchy as strongmen rule has caused the collapse of most legal institutions. Thankfully our military government and its strict hierarchy allows harsh penalties on corrupt officials... When we can find them.
strings.SAM_corruption_high_desc:
To be wealthy in an unjust society is a disgrace. Our current corruption level is high.

From the Soviet era we have inherited the institution of blat. The laws are mere suggestions; it is who one knows and how many favors one holds that grants access to resources. Taxes and bribes are seen as increasingly interchangeable. Meanwhile, smuggler rings run most industries and trade organizations.
strings.SAM_corruption_very_high_desc:
If the virtuous man is driven by responsibility, the non-virtuous man is driven by profit. Our corruption level is currently very high.

Our state apparatus has devolved into a kafkaesque nightmare of graft and patronage. All levels of government operate as extended crime families. Civilians and soldiers spend a lot of their free time keeping up with who currently runs what.

Long years of disorder have turned Russia into a country that imports much and exports little. This must change if it is to prosper once again. The Kombinats, large industrial trusts, offer a pathway to affect this change.

If they are properly supported by the state, and their industrial possessions subsidized and expanded, they can, and will, serve as a solid economic foundation for the Russia of the future.

strings.SAM_Our_Guide_desc:
As another year rolls on, our guide Andrey Vlasov continues his Sisyphean reconquest effort. Whatever power he gathers, his underlings steal. Whatever legitimacy he possesses, the German bombings strip away. The sad man grows older, buried under the weight of history and the judgement of those outside his borders. Yet he has not yet given up, for the upcoming troubles in Germany may signal his one last chance.

For now, his greatest quality is that he is able to maintain a coalition. The various generals like him better than they like one another and the people have found his rule fair if not particularly noteworthy. There are worse places in Russia than Samara, certainly. But if Vlasov is to serve as a guide to a renewed Russia, he must begin anew his consolidation of military and popular support.
strings.SAM_Our_Voice_desc:
Our consolidation effort goes through Miletiy Zykov. Zykov is difficult to describe, for much of his past is cloaked in mystery. Few claim to know where he comes from. The man himself claims to have been a leading ideologue in the opposition to the Soviet government, and he has indeed shown himself to be a highly talented public speaker and propagandist. His effort to reach the people of Russia in general, and Samara in particular, have done much to generate what few shreds of good reputation we possess. Zykov is among the greatest advocates of freedom and democracy in our officer corps, and he has built himself a small clique around this position. His aim is not merely to free Russia from both warlordism and from the Germans, but to bring forth a new, carefully supervised democracy. To many militarists in our government, he is a soft man. To German loyalists, he is a decadent parasite intent on betraying our German benefactors.

Few are sure where Zykov comes from, and few can claim to know his real endgame. But at this critical juncture, his skills in propaganda are irreplaceable. We need his voice as the army of liberation marches onwards.
strings.SAM_Our_General_desc:
There is in theory a hierarchy to the National Liberation Army, with Vlasov at the top and a range of officers neatly arrayed below him. In practice, however, the opinion of the officer corps as a whole is critical to our endeavors. And the officer corps and its committee has a champion in Sergey Bunyachenko. A former Soviet officer, Bunyachenko was captured by the Germans in the Second World War and thrown into a penal colony for his troubles. Few in Russia mourned his fate, as he was widely blamed by the Soviet leadership for losing several critical battles in the opening stages of the war.

In the dark days of the West Russian War, Bunyachenko was offered a way out of his jail sentence: join the Russian Army of National Liberation and push the WRRF back. Angry at the Soviet leadership and desperate to leave his prison, Bunyachenko agreed, and quickly rose through the rank of the National Liberation Army. Bunyachenko is widely seen as a capable officer, beloved by the men for standing up for their ideas. The general cares for little but the reunification of Russia, the annihilation of the Soviet remnant, and most of all, the downfall of Germany.
strings.SAM_Their_Puppet_desc:
Vladimir Artsezo is a hard man to his supporters, and a broken man to others. He has little sympathy for the communist regime, defeated twice in fifteen years by the Germans. He is not a monarchist, or a democrat, for the weakness of these past regimes has brought Russia into the shackles of the failed communist regime.

The Germans have become the masters of Europe, and what of it? For Artsezo and his supporters, Berlin has crushed every Jewish regime that had obscured man's progress. Vlasov and his ilk might see the Germans as means to an end, but Artsezo knows better. He sees Vlasov as a broken, pathetic man squirming to get out from under the German shadow.

Vladimir Artsezo is happy to collaborate with Germany. He sees no greater purpose than helping to enforce the German will upon the ruins of the Soviet Union, and his eager collaboration has let him secure many contacts in RK Moskowien and beyond. Vladimir Artsezo may be a hard man, or a broken man, but he is certainly a dangerous man. And an essential one, for through him Samara secures essential supplies from the German ogre.
strings.SAM_It_Never_Ends_desc:
The sound of planes overhead has become a regular occurrence for those in West Russia to the point we have learned to plan around them, bar the occasional break from their bombing schedule or unexpected change in target. Yet, the sound of a screaming payload landing on our territory is still a terror for our people. It is an agony we can only endure.

And yet, the winds of change might still be blowing. Were Germany to fall into trouble of its own, perhaps these might be the last months of the accursed terror bombings? As such, an officers' conference has been gathered to discuss how best to prepare for the upcoming window of opportunity. Various factions make their case to Vlasov and other officers.

In the meantime, regular salvaging efforts continue. Buildings torn down by the war machine see their components moved to new places. The odd supply convoy used as target practice is pushed out of the road so others may pass. Life in Russia goes on.
strings.SAM_Take_What_is_There_desc:
At the conference, Zykov and his supporters have fiercely defended their position on both ideological and coldly pragmatic grounds.

Their argument goes like this: increasing taxes on the population will drive it further away from us, and the Army of National Liberation can scarcely afford to lose what few hints of goodwill it still has. Accepting more German weapons is also not a good plan, as our soldiers must be seen and known as liberators of Russia, instead of mere German puppets. Thus, the best, and hardest path according to Zykov is to make do with what we have. This will leave us weaker in the short term. But being loved by our people and embraced by those we liberate will be incredibly helpful.
strings.SAM_Scavenge_for_Vehicles_desc:
Zykov might have convinced the rest of the officer corps and its various factions not to increase supply requisition on the people, nor supply demands to the Germans, but there is still a tangible shortage in almost everything. The most pressing concern is our ever dwindling pool of motorized vehicles. Without much native industry and with limited import capacities, our fleet of trucks and armored vehicles melts by the day.

Our men have been sent to scour the countryside for anything that might roll downhill. Tractors that peasants have given up on, military cars and trucks that have been abandoned in the wood, whatever broken down German or Soviet tank hidden in marshes or forests. This iron harvest will be a meager one, and most of what we find will likely be useless. But any quantity of engine blocks and armor plate we can scrounge up will be useful for the cause.
strings.SAM_Looking_For_Treasure_desc:
With the drain on our vehicle fleet somewhat arrested, our soldiers are moving their efforts to whatever else can be lifted and carted off to our bases. Forgotten German or Soviet supply caches, farms abandoned by fleeing or dead peasants, downed German planes, buried Tsarist gold...

The pile of junk brought back to the bases is sifted through by the men. Whatever we can use is stashed away. Among the rest, whatever has a monetary value is hauled to convoys headed for the Moskowien border, where black market traders will give us a fraction of its price for our trouble. Selling abandoned cuckoo clocks and teapots will not make us rich men, but anything we can trade on the black market for supplies will still prove to be of value.

To cheer up the soldiers, fifteen percent of every discovery's value Is given to the men directly to encourage them to search. Of course, any soldier that steals from civilians to increase his stash shall be shot. The idea is to avoid angering them further, not use them to pad our retirement funds.
strings.SAM_Take_What_is_Ours_desc:
Bunyachenko and a sizable fraction of the officer corps have rejected Zykov's idea of sparing the population further taxes. It's unfair for the soldiers to risk their life and live on stale rations as the people of Samara live in peace and quiet. The citizens must be better integrated into our governmental structure, to enable them to give their fair shake. They've had the luck of being among the first to be liberated by the KONR, and they should be aware of this.

Bunyachenko's plan is thus to organize a detailed census. Once the population of every village and community is known to us, we can begin estimating how closely the sheep can be shorn without injuring them. This is a big undertaking, and it will occupy most of our soldiers as well as all of our men with accounting skills. But the reward will be well worth it.
strings.SAM_The_People_Provide_desc:
Crates of food. Bags of grain. Boxes of ammunition. Scavenged rifles. It's all coming in!

With little use for money in the past decade, many have chosen to pay their taxes in kind to their local garrison. Military accounts are present at every step of the way to ensure that every citizen is giving their fair due to the army: enough of their surplus for the army to be fed, but not enough taxes as to ruin the citizen.

Some of our poorer citizens have instead given time to the army, paying their dues through twice a month corvees. Their time has been centered in the workshop where guns and ammo are manufactured. Others have cleared new plot of land to grow food for soldiers on. A few have just been drafted as reservists, and given a little food for their troubles.

As they want to, many complain about the rise in taxes. But not too loudly, however, for the taxman is also the military keeping order.
strings.SAM_The_Russian_People_Deliver_Us_desc:
Our men have never been this well fed or supplied. Their morale has skyrocketed as a result, and now many apply to join our army to escape the grinding poverty of the Russian Anarchy. Our warehouses are filling up, and our cooks spend days cooking surplus grain into hardtack for further campaigns abroad.

The citizens have not shared much in this excitement. But even the most skeptical has to admit that the newly reinvigorated army is doing more than ever to earn its pay, increased as it may be. Patrols on the road are more frequent. Bandit operations are increasingly seeing crackdowns. A cynical man might say this is to eliminate competition to our tax collectors. But everyone admits that Samara has never been a safer place. The Russian people have given us the tool we need to deliver them from their troubles. Soon, perhaps, military order and prosperity will reign from the Baltic Sea to the Pacific.
strings.SAM_Take_What_is_Theirs_desc:
Against Bunyachenko and Zykov stands Artsezo's faction of officers and German “advisors.” Why bother to scavenge for rusted Soviet firearms and moldy turnips covered in cow shit while Samara's useless peasants hide their bounty underground? The KONR is blessed with access to the greatest military superpower the world has ever seen. Why not make use of it? Every shipment of quality German arms and supplies is another advantage that the Liberation Army cannot go without.

Artsezo's proposal has gained quite a bit of support beyond his own limited circle. For some Zykovites, getting weapons and supplies from the Germans means avoiding further taxation on the people. For some of Bunyachenko's faction, the prospect of new ammunition for their German weapon supply is very attractive indeed. However, those not in favor of the plan argue from many angles, that depending on the Germans is a bad plan in the long run, and that continually begging for equipment is unsightly. In the background, the German advisors observe the unfolding debate.
strings.SAM_German_Arms_desc:
To the German's credit, the shipments came rapidly, and in considerable quantity. But rapid delivery and quantity of shipped equipment is perhaps the only thing that can be said about the German aid.

Soldiers have spent days unpacking crates after crates of World War Two era Kar98k rifles and 7.92x57mm Mauser ammunition. The Germans have supplemented their generous supply of antiquated weaponry and ammunition with stale rations. Optimists argue that they're from the West Russian War, and are still edible. Pessimists claim they're left over from World War Two.

Artsezo and his supporters do not seem to mind this. Food is food, and weapons are weapons. An army wins or dies based on discipline and leadership, and KONR has both in spades... or at least it would, if not for the whining and negative attitude of its current officer corps. One ought not to need anything stronger than a bayonet to clear communist rabble, degenerate democrats, and alcoholic bandits.
strings.SAM_Moskowien_Contacts_desc:
The shipments from the Reich will prove invaluable. But perhaps there is still more we can obtain through German help. Of course, the German government is often busy, and so it is time for us to talk to other German friends.

Across the border lies Reichskommissariat Moskowien, the vast German administration built to administer Russia west of the A-A line. Its hardscrabble population of settlers, military garrisons, and Russian second class citizens try to make a living in the shadow of the warlords and bandits that lurk beyond the border. Over the year, members of the KONR such as Artsezo have built up contact with citizens' militias and military officers of Moskowien. In exchange for help and support to Samara's government, the KONR has done its best to monitor its section of the border. Now that the German bombing campaign might be coming to an end, why not ring up our associates beyond the border and request more supplies, lest hordes of Bolsheviks, anarchists, and bandits pour over our border?
strings.SAM_Dealing_with_Dissent_desc:
It has not escaped Vlasov and the KONR leadership's attention that our Army of National Liberation is wildly unpopular even among the members of our “nation” that we have already “liberated.”

Ignoring for the moment issues of taxation we may or may not have exacerbated, the people of Samara disdain us as foreign stooges. Many citizens, especially among the left leaning, see us as unrepentant traitors that have contributed to the failure of the WRRF.

Opinion among the officer corps as to the best solution run the usual gamut of proposals. It would thus be for the best to convoke another meeting of the general staff to discuss the issue, and perhaps settle on one strategy to secure the good will of the people... or at least the absence of their opposition.
strings.SAM_The_Smart_Way_desc:
The indefatigable Zykov has used his time at the podium to argue that the best way forward is to go at it intelligently and legitimately try to improve the lives of our citizens. Legitimacy is derived from the people's support, and our soldiers are still brothers, fathers, and sons. The men tilling the fields and building the guns are no less indispensable than the men fighting for a new Russia. Enslaving a whole nation for their purposes was the mistake of the Soviet Union and of the Third Reich, and now the first is long dead and the second finds itself dying.

It might not be the easiest path. Fear, suspicion and shattered hopes push many of our citizens towards distrust. Some may never forgive us for working with the Germans, and we will have to go the extra mile to prove our good intents. But this problem must be solved now, lest our reputation of tyranny spread to newly liberated provinces.
strings.SAM_Hearing_the_People_Out_desc:
Our community outreach has gotten some results, despite the cynicism of most of the officer staff. Soldiers have begun to renovate roads in rural communities and helping to clear rubble. Peasants have, at first, been reluctant to bother the soldiers, but a few have since come out seeking help with other tasks. The soldiers have obliged to the most pressing ones, and as a result quite a bit of good will has been founded.

In parallel to this, a series of mixed civilian-military tribunals have been established. People wronged by our soldiers or government are encouraged to register their complaints with the judges. While it is out of the question to punish our soldiers too harshly - lest we lose control of the state - ensuring that the worst excesses are penalized and that aggrieved citizens are compensated goes a long way. Another idea that is slowly gaining traction are mixed military-civilian community councils, where small garrisons see their organization enmeshed with the village they protect. It will be a long process, but getting the people to support and back our cause now has a good chance of actually happening.
strings.SAM_The_Easy_Way_desc:
The accursed Bolshevik Lenin once quipped that the average citizen is only three meals away from revolution. Food uncertainty and boredom are among the best way to let a group of docile lambs get turned into scheming wolves.

Bunyachenko and many other among the Officer Committee have suggested a simple plan: buy and distribute vast quantities of foods. Living on the edge of starvation is the sad normal in the Russian Anarchy, and simply keeping our people well fed will generate generous amount of positive apathy. While Zykov is not wrong that the population needs to cooperate with our liberation project, it's not worth investing that much effort into improving their life. Better to simply leave them to their own devices, content and fed while the soldiers busy themselves with national liberation.

Acquiring the food will cost money, of course. But with the upcoming wars, a great amount of opportunities will present themselves. Our coffers can be refilled once the wars begin.
strings.SAM_Food_for_All_desc:
Having a steady pipeline of food imports and purchases coming in is one thing. Making sure it's distributed equally and without corruption or losses is quite another.

Like many Russian successor states, our woeful infrastructure has decayed considerably since the Soviet Era through lack of maintenance and terror bombings. But when there's a will, there's a way. We already garrison soldiers throughout all of our territories, and these men have to be supplied anyway. By using our extensive logistics infrastructure, we can make sure no village or community is left behind. This will require much carting over of food through difficult terrain by foot or by horse. The peace and quiet earned by making sure every single citizen is well fed will make this struggle well worth it.
strings.SAM_The_Hard_Way_desc:
Of course, helping the peasants or feeding them to earn their compliance both assume that their opinion is worth anything. The Army of National Liberation gives its life to defend the people from bandits and Bolsheviks. Those ungrateful enough to betray us are no better than traitors.

Artsezo and a few hardliners have dismissed the matter of rebellious citizens with a proposal for a crackdown. Unleash the troops on seditious communities. Throw suspected communist infiltrators in jail. Beat down protests violently. There's a life and death war out there, and softness has already condemned Russia in all four of its major wars of the 20th century. Would a mighty bear care for the opinions of worms? The National Liberation Army will secure its rear with brutal efficiency.
strings.SAM_No_Soup_for_You_desc:
Repression has had its days, and many skulls were cracked. Now after stamping out the embers of discontent, the time has come to douse them for good.

Artsezo and Zykov had a good point when they discussed the precarious food condition of the population. It's a damn shame that so many of our loyal citizens go hungry while Bolshevik pigs gorge themselves on no doubt ill acquired food. Time for some redistribution, so beloved by left wing bandits. By seizing food from problem areas and redistributing it to loyal citizens, we will simultaneously reward patriots and starve out bandit communities. The population will learn that to oppose us means going hungry.

This will teach the rabble its proper place.
strings.SAM_Our_Loyalty_desc:
A coherent domestic policy has been chosen as has a method of obtaining new equipment for our men. Now the biggest hurdle remaining to us is the question of leadership.

To some, Vlasov is a great leader, simply buried by the weight of years. For others, Vlasov is a temporary solution until the Army of National Liberation can choose its true goal and methodology. Finally, for a loud minority, Vlasov is a weak failure that is the main reason that KONR has been rotting in Samara for an entire lost decade.

A final leadership conference then. To determine where the loyalty of our men shall fall, and to finally choose what vision of Russia the KONR is truly fighting for.
strings.SAM_To_the_Committee_desc:
The KONR and its leading officers fought hard to break the communist menace. Our men bravely led the spear into the heart of the resurgent Soviet Union. Have the people been grateful to us for saving them of renewed Bolshevism? Not for an instant. Have the Germans done anything but throw us a bone before kicking us back into the kennel? In their arrogance they call us subhumans one moment before begging us to guard their borders the next.

These are hard times in Russia, and they call for hard men. The Russian Army of National Liberation will lead Russia to its renewal. Those strong enough to follow us as soldiers and generals will gladly be accepted. The others are not worth the dirt they stand on. Our leader Vlasov can have no successor but Bunyachenko.
strings.SAM_To_the_People_desc:
What is the KONR, if not means to an end? We fight for the glorious liberation of Russia! What are the Germans, if not dangerous tools at best, cruel jailers at all times!? We fight for a new, free Russia! One not enchained by the Bolsheviks, nor one enslaved to the broken German eagle. Our legitimacy comes from the strength of our army, and the strength of our support by the population. With just and wise men at their front, the Russian people shall rise to new heights of glory!

Zykov and his faction know that they are the best possible successors to Vlasov. The old general has fought to free Russia, and Zykov will see to it that the nation rises from its ashes.
strings.SAM_To_the_Reich_desc:
Woe to the conquered!

Twice now the Russian people have weakly clung to their Bolshevik masters, losing both times to the German war machine. The KONR fought bravely in the West Russian War, and was instrumental in breaking the morale of the cowardly communist hordes. Now, beyond our border the leftists plot. In this they are joined by democratic rabble and Tsarist relics. Russia has received nothing from these failed regimes but tears, blood and ash. It is indeed the time for strong men, and the Germans are strong. We must aid them in their quest to bring forth a new era. The foreign Judeo-Bolsheviks and their traitorous accomplices will hang, and from their bodies a new state will be built. Artsezo and his associates will enact this future.
strings.SAM_Who_Shall_Stand_Beside_Vlasov_desc: The factions have made their cases. For some, this was accomplished through speeches to the assembled officers and soldiers. For others, it was through demonstrations and more practical work. Three visions of our missions have made their case and argued for their methods. It is now the time to decide who shall stand beside Vlasov, and earn a place in history as successor to the future liberator of all Russian people.
strings.SAM_Rebuilding_Samara_desc:
Even though we were considered as significant assets by our benefactors to the west, we are not spared of the terror bombing campaign that the Luftwaffe has conducted indiscriminately for years. Our cities, our factories and our homes were destroyed by the bombing runs, being rebuilt only to be hit again.

The people of Samara suffered for years, with no end to the bombings in the horizon. However, we must persevere on. It is time again to rebuild the city and all our territories as well. Houses, factories and infrastructure like roads will be repaired or built to serve the people of Samara. Hopefully, this will show the people how much the KONR cares for them and what they do for them. Popular support is, after all, a key to keeping control.
strings.SAM_The_Zykov_Plan_desc: Industry is the backbone of any modern nation. Without it, we cannot have a good standard of life or develop our military, both vital parts of the Russian state. Miletiy Zykov, a reformist within the KONR's ranks, has proposed an ambitious economic plan that, if it succeeds, could bring Samaran industry to a new level. Zykov has laid plans for the construction of new factories across our territories, using investment from the civilian sector, that will hopefully have trust in our economy, to empower the military-industrial complex of our military. It is a sound plan, and we hope it will be quite helpful for our struggling economy.
strings.SAM_Develop_Samara_desc: As we begin to rebuild the city of Samara, the center of power for our state, it is important to not merely repair the ruins. We must go even further; the city of Samara before the war or the bombing runs began will look like a small town in front of the newer, reborn city. New industries, from factories to stores, will be built and supported by the government to encourage economic development; residences to house more Russian citizens will also be constructed. Our end goal is to make Samara nothing less than a shining beacon of development in West Russia.
strings.SAM_Connecting_Our_Lands_desc: Admittedly, the links between Samara and the other towns and villages under our protection are weak. Of course, the relentless bombing campaign has been the main reason behind this, and so it is imperative that with the end of the bombings we rebuild infrastructure, from roads to railways to connect our territories. Old Soviet roads will be repaired and new ones will be built, always under the funding and supervision of the government. This way, our citizens will enjoy much easier transport and our garrisons will be able to function better.
strings.SAM_Making_a_Better_Samara_desc: Our development of our capital city continues smoothly, as it continues to grow to levels only seen in the days before the collapse of the Bolshevik regime. It is the duty of the Committee to continue this valuable work for the good of the citizens. We will finish this ambitious project we have embarked on, as we are determined to do so. The city of Samara shall be the largest and most glorious city in West Russia, a monument to the Committee of National Salvation's government and their work for the common people.
strings.SAM_Creating_an_Arms_Industry_desc: Ever since the formation of our state right on the German frontier, the Reich has been our main and only benefactor; they have provided us with weapons and supplies, not to unify Russia but to remain loyal and cause trouble. However, we cannot remain dependent on them for long. It is finally time to work to achieve autarky. The Russian war industry shall be rebuilt, far better than the Bukharin years, to become the driving force behind the reunification of the country under no one but us.
strings.SAM_We_Need_Weapons_desc: Soon, our army will begin a campaign, aiming to reunify the Russian lands under one banner. To ensure that this campaign is a success, a further expansion of the arms industry is highly important. More factories will be built with the resources we have, dedicated not to civilian goods, but to producing any kind of military equipment, which will be quickly funneled to our armed forces. Guns, tanks, artillery, whatever is needed from our army, will be produced in this new, rapidly developing industry. When our armies are well-equipped, and our depots are full of supplies and arms, we will be ready to strike, and Russia will come under our fold.
strings.SAM_Preparing_for_the_Unification_desc: As the dawn of the wars for the reunification of Russia comes closer every day, it is time to make the final preparations to be ready to strike. Our economy is blossoming, as we cautiously plan its growth and more and more economic enterprises appear, further supporting the city. Now, we are in the final stretch before our reconquest begins. The Samaran government now needs to act carefully, and make its last steps before its economy and society change completely, perhaps irreversibly, with the war of reclamation.
strings.SAM_A_New_Samara_desc: With every day that passes, Samara comes closer to reclaiming its spot in the global stage. Our industry is rapidly growing, with both the military and financial sectors expanding to accommodate the needs of the government and people. Our economy has stabilized, with the people happy at their situation and with work to put food on the table every day. Our army is equipped, trained and more ready than ever to fight for their fatherland, against any enemy that dares to challenge us. We are unstoppable, and the reunification of Russian lands, fractured for decades, is finally on the horizon again.
strings.SAM_The_Committee_Plan_desc:
In the most recent years, Samara has been caught, quite honestly, lacking. Our industry is not quite what it once was, and our people are unemployed or working unproductively all across the board. It is simply impossible for us to keep our nation alive without creating a Samara more industrially efficient and capable of projecting our power across Russia. To rid our country of those too stupid to rule themselves and bring from the fractured mess a unified state, we must rid ourselves of our reliance on Germany to fashion a state from which we can enrich Russia (and in doing, ourselves).

Those who can work, will go the factories, mines, and construction teams. Those who are strong of mind and body will join the ROA.

Together, we will bring together Russia once again from the horde of squabbling warlords who have squandered the Russian dream, and return Russia to its former place in the eastern sun!
strings.SAM_Creating_Civilian_Industry_desc:
No state can call itself a country without a functioning civilian industry. The single most important building that will distinguish us from the tribes to our east will be the standard of our civilization. We shall build from the ashes a strong civilian industry, one capable of fueling a war machine itself capable of returning Russia to a strong, free nation.

Under the command of our efficient network of bureaucrats, work crews from all over Samara shall labor to create a civilian industry that will rival that of any uncivilized warlord state, one that will allow us to realize our Russian ambitions...
strings.SAM_Making_an_Efficient_Samara_desc:
We cannot have a truly efficient country, greased to the bones, unless we cut costs, reduce unnecessary spending, and liquidate all inefficient positions. Some will consider this counterintuitive in our goal of increasing efficiency, but the true goal here in one thing: creating a system that needs as little as possible to run, a system truly built on the principles of self-reliance and efficiency. With less spent on unnecessary bureaucratic expenditures, we can focus on new projects, from roads, to industry, to radar defences.

We have seen the results of a strong bureaucracy; that is a nation that slowly strangles itself from the inside. Money does not come out of nowhere, to fund our military and new very ambitious plans, we will have to break down the state apparatus to only what is absolutely necessary; the money demands we do.
strings.SAM_Let_us_Build_Roads_desc:
Within Samara there exists a lack of infrastructure, a debilitating issue that plagues our every goal. Goods from one part of the nation arrive too slowly; reinforcements arrive days after skirmishes begin, finding nothing when they arrive; in the Spring months movement stalls nearly to a halt as the mud fills the roads, rendering all but the most major roads impassable. Do we wish a strong Samara? One capable of creating a strong Russia? Then this all must change.

We will embark on an ambitious road-building campaign. Using soldiers, unemployed civilians, and construction companies, we shall pave over many of our nation's roads. As we pave these roads, we also shall pave our way to a new age, an age in which Russia can finally regain its rightful place in the sun.
strings.SAM_A_Military_Industrial_Complex_desc:
In Samara there a great many things we lack, many of which we have since learned to live without. However, there are a great deal of these things that we simply can no longer afford to live without. As shipments from Germany become rarer and rarer, and their support goes from less-than-genuine to barely even lip service (not to mention the terrible instability in Germany), we must begin to produce our own military equipment.

Incentives will be set up to encourage industrial companies across our small but strong state to open up new locations and produce more armaments. We will provide to them funding, laborers, areas to open new factories, and lucrative deals that will encourage them to produce for us. In addition we will ensure that no one company gains a monopoly by encouraging strong but healthy competition between these forces. By staying true to our beliefs in a free but government-sponsored and efficient industry, we will prove to Russia our system's superiority!
strings.SAM_Motorized_Contracts_desc:
While our armies stand strong and march to victory, that is part of the problem. Much of our army remains non motorized or only motorized on paper, with many having to slowly march to get into action. In the modern age of lightning warfare leg infantry has been made obsolete and we must understand such. If we wish to see our flag fly from the capital of a free Russia, the first step is modernizing our army.

We shall contract out to various Samaran automobile factories orders of hundreds of trucks and jeeps to equip our many infantry divisions for the fight that is surely soon to come. By contracting to multiple factories we can hope that they will compete to create more efficient vehicles, and the one that shows it can produce motorized equipment at the highest capacity and quality will receive the most funding from the Samaran government. Our goal is nothing less than the reunification of Russia and a strong all-Russian army. Let us drive into the horizon where a bright future awaits!
strings.SAM_Radar_Defences_desc:
Despite the halt in German bombings, allowing us to finally come into our own as a potential custodian of the Russian future, we worry that while the people of Samara no longer awake in the wee hours of the morning to the “death whistle” of German munitions, this new situation may at best be tentative. Instead, we must prepare for the worst while hoping for the best for all the Russian people.

Using slightly antiquated radar technology “bought” from a German base in the RK Moskowien and then duplicated in Samara, we will set up radar stations across our borders at key military installations to keep a careful watch over our people and their safety. We cannot allow ourselves to be caught off guard in this age where warfare is driven by what is in the air as much as it is our legions on the ground.
strings.SAM_Making_A_Greater_Samara_desc:
After no small effort, both by the people of Samara and their ever-present benevolent guides, the city of Samara has been completely rebuilt and re-industrialized. Now, it has reached a record level of industrial production! Droves of Russians, from disgraced wretches and invalids to able-bodied teenagers, are employed in our newly constructed arms factories. Churning out dozens of firearms and bullets a day, these factories have not only begun to lower unemployment, but have also allowed our city to better supply the army's ever increasing demand for weapons.

Hurrah for the committee! Hurrah for the Russian Liberation Army!
strings.SAM_The_Officer_Plan_desc: Kickstarting Samara's economy in time for the reclamation of Western Russia will be no easy task. Indeed, for most people it would be impossible, but Vladimir Artsezo is not most people. Working with the most loyal elements of the ROA, he has drafted a plan that would employ the military's best commanders in the reconstruction effort. Each commander will be given a territory to govern. They will be responsible for raising conscripts and extracting goods and resources from their territories. Critics of this plan have called it modernized feudalism. Artsezo and his supporters know that it is just common sense.
strings.SAM_Put_the_Women_to_Work_desc: Rebuilding Russia will take the effort of every single child of the Motherland. While the sons of Russia are fighting to retake their nation there must be someone to keep the factories running and finish the repairs. It is time for the daughters of Russia to prove their loyalty and dedication to our cause. The women of Samara will trade their aprons for uniforms, and the kitchen for the factory floor. We cannot afford the niceties of traditional roles in modern war. Our enemies are totally committed to our destruction, so our commitment to victory must be total as well. Every last citizen of the nation will do their part for the war effort.
strings.SAM_Integrated_Civilian_And_Military_Sec: Our industry is a disorganized jumble of state-owned and private factories producing a mixture of civilian and military goods. We have made do with this so far, but it will not do any longer. We must integrate the civilian and military economies, placing both under the control of the ROA to make sure that our army is always kept well supplied. Under military oversight, we will be able to rapidly expand our industry in an organized manner that serves our needs above those of some capitalists who are more concerned with their profits than national redemption. The officers have not steered us wrong yet and there is no reason to believe they will do so now.
strings.SAM_Guns_for_the_Motherland_desc: Weapons are and always have been the key to war. Without them, we cannot do anything on the battlefield, and so our leader has announced that a further expansion of our capacity to produce them is required. Some will be built in new factories as our industry continues to grow, while others will be scavenged from the old Soviet military, nearby warlord states or even old German equipment. With sufficient equipment, the Russian Liberation Army will be able to crush any opposition, whether that be bandits or opposing warlords.
strings.SAM_Bigger_Guns_for_Our_Boys_desc: Our officers call artillery the queen of the battlefield for a reason. Much like the queen on a chess board it is equal parts powerful and useful. Artillery is essential to modern warfare. It can break an entrenched enemy or halt an offensive in its tracks. Now that we have the industry to keep our troops supplied with the basics of equipment, such as rifles and ammunition, some of our regional commanders have turned their production to heavier guns. While the warlords to our north are stuck with hordes of men who are lucky if they have a machine gun, our troops will be backed by lines of cannons that will bring down thunder and death on all who stand in our way.
strings.SAM_I_Want_Planes_desc: Another critical part of war, at least in the modern age, is the war in the air. Having a functioning air force can be a major advantage in the battlefield, especially in Russia where they are a precious resource. A Samaran air force to accompany the Liberation Army will be a massive improvement to our military, and will allow us to attack and bomb any enemy that appears in our way with ease. At least, that's what our leader claims. As for the source of these planes, he has suggested we reach out to German contacts and ask for a few old aircraft from the days of the Second World War, that we can then use and refurbish for our own purposes.
strings.SAM_They_Need_Bases_desc: Planes, in order to function well, always need extensive facilities on the ground. To aid our air force, we have decided to construct a new base for the Samaran air force, a good distance from our capital. Composed of a series of different buildings and runways to accommodate the proud Russian air fleet, this shall be a good step for the future expansion of this branch of our military. Should the Committee approve it, a significant share of our military budget will be directed there due to its importance.
strings.SAM_Making_My_Samara_desc: Artsezo and the officers' plan to rebuild Samara and the surrounding regions is beginning to pay off. The commanders have become familiar with their assigned territories, and have learned how to extract the greatest value from them. For the first time in years production and tax quotas are being met, banditry has decreased, and a semblance of order has been restored. Each military governor has total control over their allotted land, and in return for their power they pledge their fealty to Artsezo and their soldiers to the ROA and the cause of Russian reclamation. Once we have eliminated our opposition we can expand this system across all of Russia, laying the foundation for a new, stronger Motherland.
strings.SAM_Now_We_Fix_Our_Situation_desc: Finally, the economy of Samara has been improved and stabilized to an acceptable point. However, while this problem might soon be solved, there is another issue to be settled. While our goal is to unify Russia under our banner, numerous factions compete for control within these lands, each with their own ideas and ambitions for a united Russia. It is time to bring an end to this. We must end the divisions and fractures laying claim to our land and eliminate these pretender states from a position of power.
strings.SAM_The_Voice_of_Reason_desc:
In the ensuing political confrontation, Miletiy Zykov, the ideological voice of the Committee and the passionate voice for democracy, achieved the goodwill of the venerable Chairman Vlasov and rose to the rank of the 'second man' in the KONR. Few expected such a contentious figure to become the designated heir to Vlasov, but it seems that his radical ideas and appeal to the people brought the head propagandist of Samara far more weight to his bid for power than his enemies could ever expect.

Of course, the favor of the old general is not enough to protect Zykov from attacks by rivalling factions. Many members of the KONR, especially the more conservative members of Artsezo's faction, have barely concealed their contempt for the “daydreaming demagogue.” The usually apolitical Bunyachenko faction have, unusually, also expressed dismay at Zykov's election. The new Deputy-Chairman has yet to prove his worth, but no matter what it takes, Zykov will make every effort to accomplish the goals the Russian liberation movement was founded upon - the overthrowing of tyranny, wherever it may be, and the creation of a new, free Russia, one without Bolsheviks and any exploiters of the Russian blood.
strings.SAM_Dealing_with_Bunyachenko_desc:
General Bunyachenko and his fellow officers do not oppose us with the same virulence as Artsezo and his clique does. However, our program is still unpopular with the officers. Many accuse us of selling out the hard working men of the ROA for ungrateful rabble that has done nothing but depict us as cowardly collaborators.

Fortunately, we have reason to think that there is still some honor and patriotism among the officers outside of Artsezo's group. The officer's clique and Bunyachenko agree with us that we need at least a small amount of popular support if we're to succeed. We must convince them that offering a democratic Russia is the best path forward.
strings.SAM_Speak_with_Bunyachenko_desc:
General Bunyachenko is long established as the mouthpiece of the officers' committee. However, it is also suspected that his apathy hides secret dreams of a renewed Russia, one able to punish the Germans and Bolsheviks both. Even more important is his influence within the officer corps, as his years of dedicated service have made him a popular, non controversial figure.

It is thus crucial that we begin talks with him, and attempt to bring him closer to our democratic aims. This will be a long ordeal, and one that may never succeed fully. However, convincing him to ask the officers' committee to give us a chance is an easily attainable first step.
strings.SAM_Speak_with_the_Committee_desc: The officers' committee is an important asset in our crusade to liberate Russia. The officers themselves hate the communists and Germans for getting us in this mess. Why not appeal to their patriotism, as well as to their ambition? While it is true that our plan is to eventually give back some power to the common man, the officers of the ROA will still be better off as respected elder statesmen of a strong, united Russia than as petty princes in a backwater military junta. Surely it is an acceptable trade?
strings.SAM_Bureaucratic_Allies_desc: We know not if Bunyachenko or our other officer contacts upheld their end of the bargain. What is known, however, is that cooperation with the officers' committee has been going a lot smoother recently. It is now time for this cooperation to trickle downwards, and reassure the fighting men that Zykov will lead them to honor, glory, freedom, as well as a decent salary bonus. After all, a poorly organized and poorly motivated army is no army at all.
strings.SAM_Dealing_with_Maltsev_desc:
Our most dangerous opposition consists of the clique of men centered around General Artsezo. Men who see the collapse of Russia not as a tragedy, but as an opportunity to get rich. Encouraged by their German sponsors, the Artsezoite seek to grind poor Russian citizens into the dirt to extract every ruble of loot from this catastrophe.

While we shall work to prevent the spread of this rot any further, a significant group of officers already think like Artsezo. We must thus deal with them, as well as with the leftover German influence in the ROA, if we're to shed away our image as unhinged collaborators among the people.
strings.SAM_Speak_with_Maltsev_desc:
General Artsezo is a hard, cynical man, unconvinced by the idea of sharing the ROA's power with it's citizens. In his little clique lay some of the fiercest opponents to our democratic ideals.

Artsezo himself is also both greedy, and indispensable. His contraband network will be of great assistance to us, and he alone can keep our opponents within the officer corps in line. Why not appeal to his greed? By asking him to help us capture all of western Russia, we can buy off his patience. The rogue general believes us to be an idealistic rabble...and can not expect us to betray him, when the time comes.
strings.SAM_Speak_with_the_Germans_desc:
Our German “friends” in Moskowien and beyond might be busy with their own troubles right now, but the sight of Russian unification on their doorsteps is sure to alarm them eventually.

We still have a little good-will with the Reich for our work in pushing back the communists and bandits. By cashing in every last contempt-drenched favor, we can reassure them that we are merely making a pre-emptive move against the WRRF. In turn, German food and supplies will help us secure our rear as we leave Samara and go off to war.
strings.SAM_Strenuous_Frenemies_desc:
Artsezo and the Germans think us weak willed and easily subverted once the time comes. Let them dream this, for our own day shall come, too.

With both factions giving us some leeway, it's time to crack down hard on corruption within the ROA. Any German bandit or smuggler caught aiding this blight on the people will be publicly shot. Junior officers, common soldiers and citizens victim to predation in the past will be compensated. By shedding the image of a decaying German junta even further we can in time earn the respect of our citizens.
strings.SAM_Making_Use_of_Vlasov_desc:
Whatever could be said about him, one cannot deny that Vlasov is, indeed, a significant person in the thousand-year-old Russian history: A living myth who will be remembered along such figures as Alexander Nevsky and maybe even Peter the Great for his decisiveness to rise against tyranny and lead the Russian people into a new, freer future. As befits any true historical hero, Vlasov's biography is full of wrongful and controversial decisions, and many deprecate him for his mistakes, but they will not be the judges of the Motherlands History.

The stagnation of the internal affairs in Samara caused many people, including both the elite of the Committee and the common Russian folk, to turn on General Vlasov for his alleged apathy to the needs of Russia and his inability to govern the KONR, but his authority among the new Russian government is still indisputable. Combined together, Vlasov's supreme power and his backing of Zykov's democratic reformist bureaucrats will become a battering ram which will break down the discontent of the KONR and open a way to the true reforms we wish to see enacted.
strings.SAM_The_Power_of_Radio_desc:
Radio is the cheapest way to reach every soldier and citizen, wherever they may be. By launching new programs that mix entertainment and education, we can better inform the people of the currently unfolding democratic revolution.

Deputy-Chairman Zykov is known for his oratorical skill and propaganda work. Let us use this asset to diminish the influence of untruths and deception across our land!
strings.SAM_A_Renewed_Spirit_desc:
A cautious optimism has descended on Samara. Has the ROA always been this popular? Of course it has! Why then are the memories of Chairman Vlasov hated? Vile rumors, of course, caused by the actions of vile underlings that have long been judged by the renewed ROA. Like the good tsar led astray by his wicked boyars, Vlasov has come to dispense justice and help to the people of Samara!

Of course, only a gullible minority preach this gospel. For the rest of the population, the ROA has simply managed to emerge renewed from its stagnation after the end of the German bombings. Curious about where we are going with this, and too cynical to oppose us violently in a quixotic effort at rebellion, our good citizens are themselves beginning to emerge out of their apathy.
strings.SAM_Begin_the_Unification_desc: With our internal situation under control, we must now begin our wars of unification. No longer mere hunting dogs for the German, we of the ROA must proudly accept our destiny as liberators of Russia. If every Russian is to live free of fear and oppression, then we must not fail! Soldiers, citizens, onward!
strings.SAM_The_Committee_Prevails_desc:
Amid a significant amount of political turmoil among Samara's elite, the committee of officers responsible for making all of our statelet's important decisions has decided its successor. Even with Zykov advocating his idealistic “democracy” and General Artsezo promoting the worst kinds of corruption, the committee has thankfully chosen the rational path and nominated Sergey Bunyachenko as the new head of the ROA.

General Bunyachenko is competent and disciplined, perfect for the continuation of the ROA's mission. His first task: to restore stability to our fractured political situation, remind the various officers who really is in charge, and begin shaping the ROA into a force capable of governing.
strings.SAM_Work_with_Zykov_desc:
Although we all accept the leadership of General Vlasov, the ROA has substantial internal factions, each with its own idea of how best to run Samara. General Bunyachenko, for instance, is a fairly standard advocate of a single-party right wing state. Zykov, on the other hand, has far more peculiar opinions. Zykov is an unabashed liberal who campaigns relentlessly for greater democratization. The fact that he had to collaborate with the Third Reich to do so does not seem to faze him.

Although we see eye to eye on very few issues, our faction and his do have the capacity to reconcile. Zykov's supporters, more than anything, desire at least surface-level improvements in the common people's situation. If we can achieve the veneer of progress, we may be able to form a mutually beneficial relationship.
strings.SAM_Nominate_Him_desc:
Miletiy Zykov is an impressively principled advocate of democracy. His soaring speeches and firm convictions make him one of our greatest assets in terms of propaganda, performing sorely needed work to rectify the Russian people's perception of the ROA as traitors and assets of the Reich. He is also a snake who should not be trusted with any position of power, lest he steer our army towards his mad dreams of liberalism.

Nevertheless, snakes have their uses. Zykov's way with words makes him the only major politician in Samara with any form of public support. Giving him a prestigious yet powerless sinecure will show the people that we have their best interests in mind, or at least convince them that we do.
strings.SAM_Celebrate_Vlasov_desc:
Ah, the great General Vlasov--what an underappreciated man! He defected from the criminal Red Army and brilliantly played the Reich in order to gain the leverage to liberate Samara from the Bolshevik scourge. Now he benevolently leads the ROA, preparing to one day liberate Russia from communism once and for all! Unfortunately, the vast majority of Samara's population does not quite see the situation this way. Most believe him to be a German toady and a traitor to the nation.

If we are to gain any sort of legitimacy, we need to combat the false narratives about our leader and founder. With the help of Zykov and his propagandists, we can tell the Russian people that Vlasov is a hero worthy of respect. In time, they may even believe us.
strings.SAM_First_Among_Equals_desc:
The officers' committee that runs Samara is a democratic institution of ROA generals committed to managing the liberation of Russia. However, as in any organization, certain figures are likely to become disproportionately prominent. General Vlasov, of course, is our most respected leader, owing to his heroism in fighting the Soviets. However, General Bunyachenko has himself rapidly risen in importance following his election by the committee.

To the uneducated masses, this might appear to be evidence that Samara is a military dictatorship, where power is consolidated in the hands of one man. This is naturally a misconception, but one that needs to be corrected to increase trust in our government. Bunyachenko is merely the first among equals, obeyed out of admiration rather than fear. At least, not yet.
strings.SAM_Demote_Maltsev_desc:
The generals of the ROA are loathed by many Russians as traitors and collaborators, and none more so than Vladimir Artsezo. Artsezo embodies every negative characterization of our organization; he is corrupt, sleazy, greedy, and infamously close to the Germans. Overall, a man of shockingly little moral fiber. He drags Samara down with every day he spends in its senior ranks, but is disconcertingly influential among some less scrupulous officers.

Neutralizing Artsezo as a powerful player in the ROA's politics is a necessity in order to limit the corrosive influence he has on our discipline and popularity. A demotion should do wonders to cut him down to size, as well as showing the skeptical populace that we are capable of dealing with bad actors within our hierarchy.
strings.SAM_Sideline_the_Germans_desc:
Out of all the brands and slanderous titles that have been applied to Vlasov and the ROA, none have been more devastating than the accusations that we are German-backed traitors to the motherland. Also quite devastating is the fact that they are entirely true. In order to strike out against the Bolsheviks, General Vlasov made a tactical alliance with the Third Reich. Inconveniently, many German advisors sent over during this period are still present and fairly visible.

The advisors have been far more trouble than they are worth. We have all the weapons we need, and the Reich is not exactly a reliable partner. In the long run, erasing all remnants of our collaboration with Germany will redeem us in the eyes of the Russian people, and our legitimacy as a nation is far more important than our reputation in the eyes of a country that seeks to keep Russia weak and divided.
strings.SAM_The_Committee_Looks_Outward_desc: Ever since the Tatars were conquered a long, long time ago, they have been an integral part of the Russian nation. However, with the unfortunate collapse of the country, they believe they have a chance to rise again. We must prove them that this is their greatest mistake. They are our neighbor, and so it shall be easy for the great Russian Liberation Army to march on and crush any hopeless resistance they offer. The time has come for this futile separatist effort to end, and for the Russian flag to fly high over Kazan once again.
strings.SAM_The_Kormchiy_Rises_desc:
Now's the time, now's the hour. The venerable Chairman Vlasov has chosen commander Artsezo as his heir. Gone are the years of stagnation and weakness. The ROA now belongs to men of action.

Much remains to be done, our hold on power is still tentative. Our rivals are still powerful. We must mold the ROA to our needs to ensure Russia's future... as well as our own interest.

The Zykovites as well as the officers committee must be put in their place. We must strike now preventively to catch them off guard. Good thing that Deputy-Chairman Artsezo has kept a long list of contacts and resources for just such a moment.
strings.SAM_Sideline_Our_Rivals_desc:
As long as Bunyachenko and Zykov plot our downfall, our political program will be in danger. We must thus sideline them to secure our position

It would be ill advised to try a power move against these men while our enemies lurk beyond the border. The best move, for now, is to begin reducing their influence and make it clear to the officers of the ROA that from now on, promotion and wealth can only come from aiding Artsezo.
strings.SAM_Erase_Their_Legacies_desc:
It's always a bit awkward to purge political rivals with long illustrious careers of service to the nation. Zykov is, if not beloved, then cautiously liked by the civilians of Samara for his propaganda speeches on democracy and the importance of a free Russia. Bunyachenko, on the other hand, is popular with the soldiers for his exploits in the West Russian War.

By beginning a campaign of propaganda, we can polish our leader's image while slowly erasing the legacy of these two trouble makers.
strings.SAM_Turn_Their_Supporters_desc:
Bunyachenko and Zykov have die hard supporters; some men really do believe in the bizarre democratic dream; others feel that an allegedly just and fair general like Bunyachenko really is the ROA's best chance at saving Russia.

Thankfully, many more officers are honest in that they chose the horse that seemed most likely to win the race. After Artsezo's ascension, these men have stayed loyal to Zykov and Bunyachenko's side out of a desire to be on the winning team when the round of musical chair end.

These men can be persuaded to change side, were we to make a better offer than their current boss. Artsezo has accumulated quite a sum of money and good quantity of land for such an occaison. By doling out payments, we can trim our rival's power for the time being
strings.SAM_Our_Eternal_Leader_desc: Our efforts against Bunyachenko and Zykov are paying dividends. While neither men are out of the game yet, their powerbase has significantly shrunk.
